title: Introduce residency-attest-wallet, per-route delegation filter, and audit-seal cache
author: Aisha Tan
description:
Motivation: Customers operating under strict data residency and regulated-key controls asked for an auditable, compact proof that a request used a region-anchored KMS key and that any operator-delegated actions were filtered by per-route policy. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a resident 'attest wallet' abstraction that binds service requests to a signed KMS-derived residency proof (compact hash chain), 2) a per-route delegation filter that projects RBAC v2 grants into least-privilege delegations and prevents operator escalation across geozones, and 3) an in-memory audit-seal cache that reduces KMS signature load while preserving non-repudiable audit chains for forwarding.

Summary of changes:
- service/attest-wallet: new package implementing ResidencyAttestWallet (creates short-lived attestations signed with region-scoped CMKs, exposes Verify/Embed APIs used at gateway and routing layers)
- gateway/middleware: add AttestWalletMiddleware which attaches attest payload to outbound responses and validates inbound claims (fallback to online verification if cache miss)
- auth/delegation: DelegationFilter that evaluates RBAC v2 decisions and emits scoped operator delegations; rejects delegations that would broaden residency scope or add cross-region service roles
- audit/forwarder: AuditSealCache which caches signed seals (KMS wrappers) for recently seen operation digests and provides TTL-based cache invalidation plus cryptographic replay-resistant proof (nonce chaining)
- integration tests and e2e harness updated to simulate multi-region KMS and operator delegation scenarios
- docs: architecture note and API surface doc for public SDK use

Checklist:
- [x] Implement ResidencyAttestWallet prototype
- [x] Implement DelegationFilter and wire into auth pipeline
- [x] Add AuditSealCache with configurable TTLs and eviction metrics
- [x] Unit tests for wallet, filter, cache
- [x] Integration tests for KMS fallback path and cache miss/rehydration
- [x] Update console schema to display attest status per-request
- [x] Add migration note for operators using legacy delegation header

Compatibility notes:
- The new wallet uses an additional header X-Redwood-Attest in internal service-to-service calls; backward compatible when header absent (wallet will attempt transparent verification via token proof).
- DelegationFilter is opt-in behind feature flag auth.delegation_projection (default: off for 72 hours rollout).

CI: initial run failed on lint (golangci) due to naming in attest-wallet; fixed in commit 3; integration flakes observed in KMS simulator (transient), added retry and a KMS simulator seed.

Migrations/deployment:
- Feature flag gate + canary rollout: start with 5% of traffic for tenant-scoped CMKs, then 25/50/100 once metrics stable
- Observability: new metrics added (attest.cache_hit_rate, delegation.filter_rejects, audit.seal_sign_rate, audit.seal_cache_ttl_evictions) and tracing spans (attest.wallet.verify, delegation.filter.eval)

Security rationale:
- Minimizes KMS usage by caching small sealed hashes rather than signing full payloads on every request
- DelegationFilter enforces residency invariants: an operator delegation cannot expand the region set for a request and cannot add roles not derivable from the base RBAC grant
- The attest proof includes a KMS signature + monotonic nonce so auditors can validate forward-only progression of attestations

- 3c4b5a: fix lint naming and add integration retry for KMS simulator
- 6d7e8f: docs and migration notes, console panel change

Files changed (high level): ["service/attest-wallet/wallet.go", "service/attest-wallet/wallet_test.go", "gateway/middleware/attest_middleware.go", "auth/delegation/filter.go", "audit/forwarder/seal_cache.go", "audit/forwarder/seal_cache_test.go", "integrations/tests/residency_e2e.yml", "docs/arch/residency-attest-wallet.md", "console/schema/requests_attest.json"]

Review thread and timeline:
- 2026-02-10 (PR opened by Aisha Tan): initial description and prototype attached
- 2026-02-11 (Connor Li): "High level looks good. Two asks: 1) add explicit TTL and staleness metric, 2) show a sample signed attestation format in docs." (author reply: implemented sample in docs and exposed attest.cache_ttl_seconds metric)
- 2026-02-12 (Marisol Vega): "Concern: how does the DelegationFilter interact with existing operator escalation whitelist? Please add unit test that simulates operator with multi-zone privilege." (author reply: added filter unit tests and guard to consult operator-whitelist; if operator is on whitelist, delegation is allowed but we emit strong audit tag)
- 2026-02-13 (Ethan Park): "CI flakes on KMS sim, consider deterministic seeds for tests and exponential backoff for signer." (author reply: added deterministic seed option and retry backoff)
- 2026-02-15 (Connor Li, approved): "Approvals from security side, minor nits addressed."
- 2026-02-16 (Merge queue): CI green, canary gating config added to deployment manifest

Notes from reviewers:
- Added suggestion to surface per-tenant attestation age in Console request inspector (implemented)
- Suggested audit retention policy: keep attest seals 90 days by default; made TTL configurable via audit.seal_cache.ttl_days

Release notes: "Added Residency Attest Wallet to produce compact KMS-backed residency proofs, a DelegationFilter for RBAC v2 projection to prevent cross-region operator escalation, and an Audit Seal Cache to reduce signing load while preserving non-repudiable audit chains. Opt-in via feature flag auth.delegation_projection; see docs for migration and console support."

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: misconfigured TTL could allow stale attestations to be accepted. Mitigation: default conservative TTL (60s for cache hits, 90d for offline sealed proofs), observable alerts on attest.cache_hit_rate drops and delegation.filter_rejects spikes.
- Risk: operator whitelist could bypass residency guard. Mitigation: whitelist changes require APPROVAL queue and are surfaced to audit with elevated retention.

Conclusion: This change provides a practical balance between cryptographic assurance for regional KMS usage and operational cost by caching short sealed proofs. It is feature-flagged and rolled out in controlled canaries. Everything merged with squash once CI passed.
